implement.approach: r8 (coordinator, on top of lane-2 r7): Round-7 adversary P1 — after 250 durable HOLDs every later receipt was answered pending forever because each HOLD replay consumed the settlement budget before the fresh receipt was looked at. Fix in reconcileOfflineReceipts(): `settlements` increments only when the RPC's delivery !== 'replayed' (the RPC is still called for every entry until the budget of new decisions is spent; replays are single indexed lookups under the owner lock and the 2 MB body cap bounds their count). Regression test pins 250 durable HOLDs + 1 fresh receipt over three drains. Round-7 P2 (device queue never chunks a >2 MB body) is a MOBILE queue concern (apps/mobile/src/data/offlineWallet.ts drain) owned by the W05-07/W04-05 mobile path and tracked there; the Edge already answers any byte-bounded batch of any length. --- lane-2 r7 approach: Started from BASE_SHA, reused the sound r6 SQL ordering (replay/conflict/HOLD before freeze, p_defer_new) and shared-types validator, wrote the r7 regression tests first (fail on base, committed separately), then implemented: Edge route byte-bounded batches + parseSyncShot normalisation of the frozen output + per-receipt HOLD of ingress-refused evidence; forward migration 20260910150000 with a private lease shot writer and gate vouch; security_regression.sql U3/U8b corrections and new U3b. Verified against disposable postgres:16 (Edge suite with ignored==0, RLS matrices fresh + upgrades), frozen deno 2.5.6 typecheck, prettier, and the AC4 base-vs-candidate proof in a separate worktree with a base-migrated DB.

residual_risks: Per-request settlement budget (OFFLINE_RECEIPT_BATCH_SETTLE_MAX = 250 in supabase/functions/api/index.ts): entries past 250 in a single POST are answered `pending` by the route without an RPC call (nothing durable written, ticket still reserved, the app keeps them queued and redelivers on the next drain — covered by a route test). This is a route-level pending for not-yet-evaluated receipts, distinct from the SQL-owned freeze pending; the objective's 'decide pending in SQL' clause is about the freeze path, but a reviewer may prefer no route-side pending at all. Removing the constant makes every entry under the 2 MB cap reach SQL at the cost of unbounded RPC round trips per request.
